description: Priority-county community knowledge holder registry for Community Knowledge Holder Partnership campaigns. Entries are role-based institution TYPES only — never named individuals. Real outreach contacts live in private operator tooling, never in the repo. Every holder carries a low-authority source classification (community_oral / self_published): submissions can inform research but can never publish alone.

counties.priorityRationale: Dense documented civil-rights and Reconstruction-era place history with thin digitized local coverage relative to national narratives.

holders.intakeNotes: Newsletters, cemetery surveys, and vertical files naming local figures and places; strongest on source citations for the sourceCitation field.
Branch meeting minutes, membership rolls where shareable, and organizer oral histories; strong on role/place/year triples.
Minute books, funeral programs, homecoming booklets, and cornerstone records tying people to a standing or former church site.
Clipping files and locally published county histories; useful for corroborating citations submitted by other holders.

counties.priorityRationale: Major movement geography where neighborhood- and congregation-level knowledge is underrepresented in digitized archives.

holders.intakeNotes: Congregation anniversaries and program booklets naming deacons, choir leaders, and founding families with dates.
Chapter histories and oral accounts of local organizers and meeting places.
Recorded oral histories; submissions should carry an oralHistoryRef with recording or transcript identifiers, never private contact details.
Funeral programs and ledgers anchoring names to dates and burial places; handle living-family details with care — never submit living persons' addresses.

counties.priorityRationale: HBCU-anchored county where faculty research and campus-adjacent community memory can surface people absent from federal archives.

holders.intakeNotes: Working papers, student theses, and departmental collections; strongest citation quality among community holders but still corroboration-required.
Marker files and county chronologies naming local institutions and proprietors.
Congregation records connecting families to church schools and burial grounds.
Chapter scrapbooks and anniversary programs documenting campus and town figures by role and year.
